summary: Microservices: React Native (Expo), Go (net/http + chi), Amazon DynamoDB database on AWS EKS (Kubernetes). It matches the team's languages and exceeds the stated budget (about $103,200-$144,300 per month).

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) matches the team's typescript skills; covers web and android and ios from one codebase; hermes and the new architecture are fast enough for most apps; is a proven choice for social projects.

alternatives.why_not: Flutter scores 0.9 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.1 points).

backend.justification: Go (net/http + chi) matches the team's go skills; handles many concurrent realtime connections well; compiled, low latency; is a proven choice for social projects.

alternatives.why_not: Elixir + Phoenix scores 2.6 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.2 points) and performance (0.5 points).
Java + Spring Boot scores 5.4 points lower overall, mainly on headroom for the expected load (5.0 points) and performance (1.0 points).

tradeoffs: No batteries, more code per feature

database.justification: Amazon DynamoDB can be placed in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), an EU region, which keeps GDPR transfers simple; single-digit ms at any scale; is a proven choice for social projects.

alternatives.why_not: Azure Cosmos DB scores 0.3 points lower overall, mainly on cost (0.4 points). Estimated infrastructure about $77,100-$114,000/month versus about $83,500-$118,400/month.
Cloud Firestore scores 4.8 points lower overall, mainly on headroom for the expected load (5.0 points) and performance (1.4 points).

tradeoffs: High vendor lock-in: Amazon DynamoDB is hard to leave once the data model and SDKs are in use.

hosting.justification: AWS EKS (Kubernetes) can be placed in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), an EU region, which keeps GDPR transfers simple; offers a 99.99% SLA, in line with the 99.99% target; tunable.

alternatives.why_not: AWS ECS on Fargate scores 3.8 points lower overall, mainly on headroom for the expected load (5.0 points) and performance (0.5 points).
Google Compute Engine scores 7.9 points lower overall, mainly on headroom for the expected load (10.0 points) and scalability (1.6 points).

tradeoffs: Needs real operations effort (patching, scaling, monitoring).
Upper cost estimate ($83,500-$118,400/month) exceeds the $80,000 budget at peak.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 25K requests/second and about 7B requests/month from 5M users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.99% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.
Cache (Managed Redis/Valkey (ElastiCache, Memorystore, Azure Cache)): about $1,000-$2,400/month

warnings.message: GDPR: keep a record of processing, sign a data processing agreement with every vendor that handles personal data, support access and erasure requests, and use standard contractual clauses for any transfer outside the EU/EEA; consider EU data residency to keep transfers simple.

A p95 of 100 ms with live updates for users spread across regions is reachable only over persistent connections (WebSockets) to servers in the users' region; avoid cold-starting functions on the hot path and load-test the fan-out at the expected 250,000 concurrent users.
The cheapest compliant option still costs about $103,200-$144,300 per month, above the $80,000 budget.

assumptions: No compatible stack fits the $80,000 budget, so cost was compared against a reference of about $123,400 per month (the cheapest compatible stack plus 25%) to keep the cheaper options ahead.
Relaxed: the monthly budget of $80,000 was exceeded because no compliant stack fits inside it.
